extra.message: This operations endpoint returns internal course and business-risk information without calling _wrk_gate() or requiring authenticated access.

cwe: CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function

extra.message: The user-controlled lane parameter is passed directly to redirect(), allowing an authenticated operations caller to generate redirects to arbitrary external URLs.

cwe: CWE-601: URL Redirection to Untrusted Site

extra.message: Attacker-supplied request data is deserialized with pickle.loads(). A caller possessing the internal token can submit a malicious pickle and execute arbitrary Python code on the server.
The endpoint writes the complete request body and Authorization header to warning logs, exposing bearer credentials and potentially sensitive payload data to log readers.

cwe: CWE-532: Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File

extra.message: Static identity verifier values are embedded in source code. Anyone with source access and the shared internal token can satisfy this verification step.

The fragment query parameter is concatenated into a Jinja2 template and evaluated with render(). A caller possessing the internal token can execute server-side template expressions and potentially arbitrary code.

cwe: CWE-94: Improper Control of Generation of Code

extra.message: The host query parameter is concatenated into a shell command passed to os.system(). Shell metacharacters allow a caller possessing the internal token to execute arbitrary operating-system commands.

cwe: CWE-78: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command

extra.message: A nonce-like code is generated with the predictable random module rather than a cryptographically secure generator such as secrets.

cwe: CWE-338: Use of Cryptographically Weak Pseudo-Random Number Generator

extra.message: The attacker-controlled length value has no upper bound and directly controls generation of an in-memory string, allowing excessive CPU and memory consumption.

cwe: CWE-789: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value

extra.message: Untrusted request XML is parsed with DTD loading, external entity resolution, and network access enabled. Malicious XML can trigger local-file access, server-side requests, or entity-expansion denial of service.

cwe: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference

extra.message: Elevated payroll and casework access is granted solely when a caller-controlled cookie or header equals the literal value lead. Any holder of the shared internal token can forge this badge and elevate privileges.

cwe: CWE-807: Reliance on Untrusted Inputs in a Security Decision

extra.message: The trace endpoint exposes the active settings module and absolute private export directory, revealing internal deployment configuration and filesystem structure.

cwe: CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor

extra.message: Django uses a known hardcoded SECRET_KEY whenever DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is absent. A deployment missing the environment variable permits attackers to forge Django-signed data.
The PostgreSQL connection falls back to the hardcoded password postgres when POSTGRES_PASSWORD is not configured.

When DEBUG is enabled—which is the default in config/settings.py—the application exposes MEDIA_ROOT through an unauthenticated static-file route. Uploaded student submissions and other protected documents can therefore be retrieved without the authorization checks in download_document().

Course resource uploads are saved without validating an extension, MIME type, or file signature. Combined with the default public media route, an instructor can upload active content such as HTML under the application origin.

cwe: CWE-434: Unrestricted Upload of File with Dangerous Type

extra.message: The CSV export iterates an unbounded Submission queryset. Django caches evaluated queryset rows, so a sufficiently large course dataset can exhaust worker memory and keep the request occupied for an excessive period.

cwe: CWE-770: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling

extra.message: User-editable names, email addresses, assignment titles, and course codes are written to CSV without neutralizing spreadsheet formula prefixes. Opening the export in spreadsheet software can execute attacker-supplied formulas.

cwe: CWE-1236: Improper Neutralization of Formula Elements in a CSV File

extra.message: API authentication checks only token equality and is_active. The APIKey model has no expiration field or maximum lifetime, so a leaked key remains valid indefinitely until manually disabled.
